name: Puppy Training Checklist
description: A puppy training checklist for owners covering house-training, crate, commands and socialization.

items.text: Choose a quiet, consistent spot for training sessions.
Stock up on small, soft, high-value training treats.
Pick a marker word or clicker to signal correct behavior.
Agree on house rules so everyone is consistent.
Set a daily routine for meals, potty, play and rest.
Keep early sessions short, around 3 to 5 minutes.
Take your puppy out first thing, after meals, naps and play.
Choose one outdoor potty spot and return to it each time.
Reward immediately the moment your puppy goes outside.
Supervise closely indoors and watch for sniffing or circling.
Clean accidents with an enzymatic cleaner to remove odor.
Avoid punishing accidents, which can create fear and setbacks.
items.note: Frequent accidents can signal a health issue worth checking with your veterinarian.

items.text: Size the crate so your puppy can stand, turn and lie down.
Make the crate cozy with a bed and a safe chew toy.
Feed meals near or inside the crate to build a positive link.
Start with short closed-door periods and build up slowly.
Use the crate for naps and quiet time, never as punishment.
Take your puppy out for a potty break right after crate time.
Teach name recognition so your puppy looks at you when called.
Practice sit using a lure and reward when the rear touches down.
Build a reliable recall with happy tones and great rewards.
Introduce down, stay and leave it in short steps.
Reward calm behavior and gentle, polite greetings.
Phase out treats gradually as commands become reliable.
Introduce new sounds, surfaces and household objects gently.
Let your puppy meet calm, vaccinated dogs in safe settings.
Expose your puppy to friendly people of different ages.
Practice gentle handling of paws, ears and mouth for vet and grooming.
Keep every new experience positive and reward calm responses.
Avoid overwhelming situations and let your puppy retreat if needed.
items.note: Ask your veterinarian about safe socialization timing before vaccinations are complete.

items.text: Let your puppy wear a flat collar or harness indoors first.
Attach a light leash and let your puppy drag it under supervision.
Reward your puppy for walking near you without pulling.
Stop walking when the leash tightens, and resume when it loosens.
Practice short, upbeat walks before long outings.
Bring treats and water for positive walks in new places.
Important: This is general information, not professional advice. Consult a professional trainer for behavior issues and your veterinarian for any health concerns with your puppy.

faq.q: When should I start training my puppy?
faq.a: You can begin gentle training the day your puppy comes home, usually around 8 weeks. Focus on short, positive sessions, name recognition and house-training first. A professional trainer can help you build a plan suited to your puppy's age and temperament.

faq.q: How long should puppy training sessions be?
faq.a: Keep sessions short, often just 3 to 5 minutes, several times a day, since puppies have short attention spans. End on a success and a reward. Frequent brief sessions usually beat one long one for keeping your puppy engaged and learning.

Many puppies are reliably house-trained within 4 to 6 months, though it varies by puppy and consistency. Frequent potty breaks, supervision and rewarding outdoor success speed things up. If you see frequent accidents or signs of illness, consult your veterinarian.

Early, positive exposure to people, places, sounds and other vaccinated dogs helps a puppy grow into a confident, calm adult. The window is widest in the first months. Keep experiences gentle and reward calm behavior, and ask your veterinarian about safe timing.

faq.q: Can I download this puppy training checklist as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. You can print it for home or download it as a PDF for your phone, so owners have training steps handy during walks, classes and daily practice with a new puppy.
